mode: no production mutation; local analysis and local simulation only

script_settings.reading: no explicit Worker CPU limit; usage_model null is not read as non-standard (version metadata already showed standard)

resume_1_analytics.tail: outcome exceededCpu, exception: Worker exceeded CPU time limit (TAIL_EVENT_ASSOCIATION confirmed)

authoritative_evidence.note: analytics status is exceededResources for both failures (the broader resource-limit category, Error 1102); only the second failure has a tail event that names CPU; the first failure has no tail and is NOT retroactively called exceededCpu

hypotheses_closed.STATIC_LOW_CPU_LIMIT_HYPOTHESIS: REJECTED: successful requests on the same Worker and versions used 310-489 ms CPU, the failures only 237.1 and 119.8 ms
hypotheses_closed.CONFIGURED_CPU_LIMIT_TOO_LOW: REJECTED: no explicit limit anywhere (repo, version metadata, script settings)
hypotheses_closed.CHAINED_WORKER_CPU_LIMIT: REJECTED: single Worker, no service binding / DO / queue
hypotheses_closed.APPLICATION_CPU_HOTSPOT: NOT_SUPPORTED: homogeneous bounded per-concept work; the concept attempt 1 died on was later processed; failures used LESS CPU than successes
hypotheses_closed.NORMAL_CPU_LIMIT_EXHAUSTION: NOT_SUPPORTED: normal CPU is hundreds of ms against a 30 s default
hypotheses_closed.TAIL_TELEMETRY_SEMANTICS_MISMATCH: WEAKENED: the analytics API (237.1 and 119.8 ms) agrees with the tail value (119 ms)

root_cause.ROOT_CAUSE_FIX: NONE_AVAILABLE (a platform bug is NOT claimed: the evidence shows an enforcement that no documented or configured limit explains, nothing more)
root_cause.failure_rate_observed: 2 platform terminations in 12 invocations; both mid-DERIVE at 10.1 s and 6.6 s wall; about 1 per 70 s of DERIVE wall time

minimum_safe_production_package.tail: keep the filtered runtime tail (outcome, cpuTime, wallTime, exceptions, status)
minimum_safe_production_package.run: ONLY crun_52632d2d-282e-44d2-aec3-a8e9f854ab2d; refetch and new run forbidden; OECD off; frontier disabled; promotion policy unchanged
minimum_safe_production_package.is_a_root_cause_fix: NO. It does not prove or fix the unexplained enforcement. It reduces the work lost per termination, the wall-time exposure per invocation and the recovery granularity; it is a bounded mitigation
files_to_change_when_authorized: tests that pin 800 / 120 / 14 invocations / 763 / 11258 (canary-limits, platform-capacity, burnin, release-manifest, migration-rehearsal artifact)

local_verification_of_the_mitigation.method: profile clone with budget 200 and lease 45 on the recorded real page, in-memory SQLite, no repository change
local_verification_of_the_mitigation.kill_sweep: kills at 10/30/50/70/90 % all resumed to the same durable state with exactly one source request
local_verification_of_the_mitigation.remaining_live_work: 108 concepts ~ 16 invocations of ~165 statements plus FINALIZE
local_verification_of_the_mitigation.expected_per_invocation_at_200: ~165 statements, ~70 ms CPU (0.42 ms per statement), ~4 s wall (about 23 ms per statement measured live: 17.5 s / 752)

lease_validation.mechanism: one lease per run taken at invocation start (UPDATE ... WHERE lease_holder IS NULL OR lease_expires_at <= now), cleared by the invocation's own final save, never refreshed in flight; units are idempotent
lease_validation.healthy_wall: 17-18 s at the 800 budget (measured); ~4-5 s expected at 200
lease_validation.overlap_possibility: a second invocation can take the lease only if the first died or ran longer than the lease; harm is bounded to duplicate idempotent work (kill and concurrency tests); the runner has no wall-clock guard, an optional guard (pause when elapsed > half the lease) would make overlap impossible

completion_odds_caveat.finding: under the stated rule 'first new exceeded* / 5xx = stop', a smaller slice does NOT raise the chance of finishing: with a hazard of about 1 termination per 70 s of DERIVE wall time, the remaining ~50 s of work gives about a 50% chance of no termination at any slice size (and if the hazard were per invocation, 16 small invocations would be worse than 3 large ones)
completion_odds_caveat.what_the_mitigation_does_buy: each termination loses at most ~7 concepts / ~165 statements instead of ~37 / ~750, and the lease wait is 45 s instead of 120 s
completion_odds_caveat.owner_decision: to make completion likely, the recovery rule could allow bounded recoveries (for example up to 3 platform terminations, each followed by waiting out the lease, then resume the SAME run; stop at the 4th or at any non-platform failure). A kill leaves a consistent durable state (proven by the kill sweeps), so this does not weaken P1 or P5. The prompt's strict first-failure-stop rule is kept in the package unless the owner changes it.

decision.RESUME_2_TECHNICALLY_READY: YES: the package is defined and locally verified; the implementation (two constants plus pin updates) is part of the authorized package and is not yet done
